rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's eighteen builder trees go (a row of ficus, jacarandas and a magnolia along the north back fences, two queen palms and a norfolk pine 3 m from the house fronts, others in the south yards); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the two swing sets, the adirondack chair, and on the open lot corners.

trees.why: the south yard with the swing set (2.8 m off): shade over the swings
the yard with the adirondack chair: a magnolia to sit under
the open lot corner at the south-west, 24 m from the walls: a full jacaranda
the south back lot line between two yards, 10 m from the houses: shade for both
the north-west back yard with the swing set (2.6 m off): a young eucalyptus over the swings
the north-east back yard, 7 m from the house: the one tree of the long back fence line, which had one every 7 m
